properties.headline: Small Craft Advisory issued November 11 at 3:12PM PST until November 13 at 1:00AM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Small Craft Advisory, south winds 15 to 25 kt
with gusts up to 35 kt and seas 9 to 14 feet expected. For the
Gale Warning, south winds 20 to 30 kt with gusts up to 40 kt and
seas 14 to 19 feet expected.

* WHERE...Coastal waters from Cape Mendocino to Pt. Arena CA out
10 nm.

* WHEN...For the Gale Warning, from 1 AM to 3 PM PST Friday. For
the Small Craft Advisory, from 9 PM this evening to 1 AM PST
Friday.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds will cause hazardous seas which could
capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A very large NW swell of 25ft at 19sec is
expected to fill into the coastal waters Friday afternoon.
Expect continued hazards through the weekend.
properties.instruction:
Mariners should alter plans to avoid these hazardous conditions.
Remain in port, seek safe harbor, alter course, and/or secure the
vessel for severe conditions.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued November 11 at 6:12PM EST until November 11 at 6:45PM EST by NWS Louisville KY
properties.description:
SVRLMK

The National Weather Service in Louisville has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Northwestern Crawford County in south central Indiana...
East Central Dubois County in south central Indiana...
North Central Perry County in south central Indiana...

* Until 645 PM EST /545 PM CST/.

* At 612 PM EST /512 PM CST/, a severe thunderstorm was located over
Riceville, or 11 miles west of English, moving east at 25 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage to
roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
English, Birdseye, Mifflin, Taswell, Eckerty, West Fork, Doolittle
Mills, Grantsburg, Sulphur and Wickliffe.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds and large
hail.

properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 11 at 1:08PM AKST until November 12 at 5:00AM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Freezing rain and rain falling on cold surfaces expected.
Total ice accumulation of a light glaze.

* WHERE...Western Kenai Peninsula.

* WHEN...From 5 PM this afternoon to 5 AM AKST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Some roads will become slick.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Areas of light rain, possibly mixed with snow,
will develop late this afternoon and become more widespread during
the evening. Temperatures will hover right around or a few degrees
above freezing through this evening. Colder areas, including hills,
bridges, and overpasses will be the most likely to see freezing
rain. Rain will then taper off overnight into Thursday morning,
with temperatures cooling to freezing or below. Thus, any water on
roadways will freeze.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. For the latest road
conditions call 5 1 1 or visit 511.alaska.gov.
